clue.text: Merely nominal followers of Simon and Peter?

parts.note: Simon Pure is a character in an 18th-century comedy whose name came to mean the genuine article, so this word follows the name Simon
Peter Simple is the title hero of a Captain Marryat novel, so this word follows the name Peter

explanation.surface: A question about whether the disciples' followers were only followers in name.
explanation.walkthrough: Simon and Peter suggest the apostles, but the clue wants the words that come after each name in two literary titles: Simon Pure and Peter Simple.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom meaning nothing more than, or simply, just as merely does.

clue.text: Make selection of burgh documents for work of fiction

parts.note: to make a selection is to pick
Wick is a Scottish royal burgh in Caithness
documents are papers

explanation.surface: Choosing papers from a Scottish town's archive to turn into a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: A burgh is a Scottish town with a charter; Wick is one, in the far north.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's first novel, The Pickwick Papers, is a famous piece of fiction.

clue.text: Decided that old city rising came first

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the word is read from the bottom upwards, so backwards

parts.note: Ur is the ancient Mesopotamian city of the Bible
a competitor who came first led

explanation.surface: Someone concluded that an ancient city's ascent happened earliest.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'rising' reads the ancient city upwards; 'came first' means led, as a winner does.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruled, as a judge has ruled, means made a formal decision or verdict.

clue.text: Public school has perfectly adequate river

parts.note: ample means quite enough, perfectly adequate
the Forth is a Scottish river flowing into the Firth of Forth

explanation.surface: A boarding school boasts that its local river is quite good enough.
explanation.walkthrough: AMPLEFORTH is a Catholic boarding school in Yorkshire; in Britain a 'public school' is a private fee-paying school.
explanation.definitionFit: Ampleforth College is a well-known Benedictine fee-paying school, the kind Britons call public schools.

clue.text: One does make trouble about church in bishop's domain

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go around the church abbreviation, holding it inside
letters made troubled are stirred up and so rearranged

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone stirs up trouble over church matters within a bishop's territory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make trouble' stirs up 'One does' as a pool, and 'about' wraps that jumble around the Church of England abbreviation; 'One' is the Roman numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: A diocese is the district under a bishop's jurisdiction.

clue.text: These fishermen have a policy, some may say

indicators.note: signals that the word is pronounced as some speakers would, so a homophone

parts.note: to have an insurance policy is to insure

explanation.surface: Fishermen claim to hold a policy, at least according to some.
explanation.walkthrough: With a non-rhotic accent the two words are said alike; 'These' points to fishermen who work near the coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Inshore fishermen work in coastal waters, so the adjective names this kind of fisherman.

clue.text: Dickensian hero's time-signal

definitions.meaning: Pip is the hero of Great Expectations, so his name with 's
the short beeps broadcast to mark the hour

explanation.definitionFit: Pip narrates Great Expectations, and the BBC's hourly radio beeps are called the pips.

clue.text: Extended sentence to make issue clear

definitions.meaning: an additional spell added to a prison term
added minutes played so that a drawn match yields a result

explanation.definitionFit: Additional time can lengthen a jail term, and football plays added periods to settle a tied game.

clue.text: Flower for a fair maid of Kent, say?

definitions.text: Flower for a fair maid of Kent, say?

parts.words: Flower for a fair maid of Kent, say?
parts.note: a beautiful girl from the cathedral city in Kent could be called a belle of that city, which names a garden bloom

explanation.definitionFit: A tall campanula with bell-shaped flowers bears the name of the Kentish cathedral city.

clue.text: Old bookmaker's items inserted in the odd hop between stops

indicators.note: the anagrammed letters are set between letters of the punctuation word, splitting it

parts.note: colons are punctuation stops

indicators.note: odd means strange, so the letters of hop are rearranged

explanation.surface: A betting man's possessions slipped into an unusual jump between halts.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'bookmaker' is a book publisher, not a betting agent. 'odd' jumbles hop, and 'between' sets the jumble inside the punctuation stops, splitting them after their third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A colophon is a printer's or publisher's emblem or closing inscription in a book.

clue.text: Surface film one lost with this rice

indicators.note: the numeral is lost, removed from the word for the surface film

parts.note: a patina is a thin film on a surface, like verdigris on bronze
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A coating has lost something and is linked with this grain.
explanation.definitionFit: Patna is a long-grain rice named after the Indian city.

clue.text: Whitehead has the advantage of a club

parts.note: the head, or first letter, of the word white
an edge is an advantage

explanation.surface: A man named Whitehead holds an advantage over a golf club.
explanation.walkthrough: Whitehead looks like a surname, but read as 'white head' it gives W.
explanation.definitionFit: A wedge is a golf club with a steep face for lofted shots.

clue.text: Reverse style and title given to Isaacson

indicators.note: reverse tells us to write the word for style backwards

parts.note: a mode is a style or manner

explanation.surface: A reversed style and a title are bestowed on someone surnamed Isaacson.
explanation.walkthrough: Isaacson reads as a surname but means Isaac's son, Esau, who was also called Edom (Genesis 25:30).
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Esau, the son of Isaac, is given the name Edom.

clue.text: Took class, I hear, when tight

indicators.note: says the word is as heard, a sound-alike of another

parts.note: a teacher who took a class taught it

explanation.surface: A teacher took a class while feeling strained, so it's reported.
explanation.definitionFit: Taut means stretched tight, as a rope is.

clue.text: Copy Eric Brant's version

indicators.note: a different version of these letters is a rearrangement of them

parts.note: the name with its S kept as a letter

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a copy of Eric Brant's version of a text.
explanation.definitionFit: To transcribe is to write out a copy of something.

clue.text: Pole alters the coda

indicators.note: the letters are altered, changed into a new order

explanation.surface: A Polish musician changes the closing passage of a piece.
explanation.walkthrough: Pole looks like a Polish person; it is an electrical pole. 'alters' rearranges THECODA.
explanation.definitionFit: A cathode is the negative electrode, one pole of a cell.

clue.text: Rear bulb for travelling show

parts.note: a lamp at the back of a vehicle that is displayed while it is on the move, not a touring circus

explanation.definitionFit: A rear lamp on a car or bicycle glows red behind it as it travels.

clue.text: Former peer, that's right

parts.note: an earl is a peer of the realm
ie, id est, means that is

explanation.surface: A one-time aristocrat confirms that something is correct.
explanation.walkthrough: IE (Latin id est) stands for 'that is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Earlier means previous or at a prior time, as former does.

clue.text: Artist attached to a craft

definitions.meaning: someone who makes pictures in oils
the line tied to a boat's bow for mooring or towing

explanation.definitionFit: A picture-maker works with a brush, and a boat's mooring rope at its bow bears the same name.

clue.text: It forms the root of sound political thinking

indicators.note: sound here means as pronounced, so the word is heard as another

parts.note: radical describes extreme political views

explanation.surface: Something forms the basis of sensible political ideas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like an adjective meaning sensible; it is the homophone signal.
explanation.definitionFit: In botany a radicle is the embryonic root of a seedling.

clue.text: Variation on a rude poem

indicators.note: a variation is a changed form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A musician plays a variation on a rude poem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Variation' takes the next three words, not just 'a rude': ONARUDE rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A rondeau is a short French verse form with a refrain.

clue.text: Country air upset no one's inside

indicators.note: the pieces sit inside the reversed word for air
in a down clue upset means turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: air as written
O is zero, nothing, no
a man is one person

explanation.surface: A rural tune is disturbed because nobody is in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns air over, and 'inside' places zero (for 'no') plus a person (for 'one') within it; the 's of one's is just 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Romania is a country in south-eastern Europe.

clue.text: This Sunday there's a handy prize for the winner

definitions.meaning: the Sunday before Easter takes its name from the fronds strewn before Christ

definitions.text: a handy prize for the winner
definitions.meaning: the frond given to a victor, and also part of the hand

explanation.definitionFit: Palm Sunday precedes Easter; the victor's frond is the palm, and the inner hand bears the same name.

clue.text: Style for a matron

parts.note: a dam is a mother, especially an animal mother

explanation.surface: A fashion suited to a mature woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Adam style is the 18th-century neoclassical design of the Adam brothers.
explanation.definitionFit: The neoclassical manner of architect Robert Adam is known by his surname.

clue.text: Cautious, accountant-very Scottish !

parts.note: CA is a chartered accountant
gey is Scots for very

explanation.surface: An exclamation that an accountant is very Scottish and careful.
explanation.definitionFit: Being cagey means being guarded and wary about giving anything away.

clue.text: Corruption in joint-stock operation for plant growth

definitions.meaning: joining a shoot onto rootstock so that it grows

explanation.definitionFit: Illicit gain from office has this name, and so does a horticultural splice of scion to stock.

clue.text: Carriage for a water-baby?

annotationWithheld.why: Carriage for a water-baby? (4): the clue plainly gives PRAM (a baby carriage, and also a flat-bottomed boat), but the answer is held as GRAM, which no reading of the clue gives

clue.text: He gets the message admittedly

parts.note: the radio word said to admit receipt of a message is also a man's name

explanation.surface: A man confesses that he has understood.
explanation.definitionFit: In radio procedure the word means message received and understood, and it is also a boy's name.

clue.text: He wants to stand Frank a tea-almost!

parts.note: frank means candid

indicators.note: almost means the word falls one letter short of complete

parts.note: tea as written

explanation.surface: Someone wants to buy a man called Frank a cup of tea, nearly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stand' means stand for election, not stand someone a treat; 'almost' drops the last letter of TEA.
explanation.definitionFit: A candidate is someone seeking office, who stands in an election.

clue.text: Moody way of painting-unbalanced

parts.note: tempera is painting with pigment bound in egg
mental is slang for mad, unbalanced

explanation.surface: A temperamental artist's technique is described as unhinged.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone temperamental has unpredictable moods.
